verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's own docs show deployment versioning: each deploy creates a code version, and runs are pinned to the version they started on. Automations are code deployed through the CLI or a GitHub Action, so versioning is a real product capability. Review depends on the user's Git workflow, which is a workaround. Waitpoint approvals pause runs at runtime and are not change review. missing for 10: documented rollback to a previous deployment version, a built-in review/diff of automation changes, independent corroboration of versioning behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: When a task run starts it is locked to the latest version of the code (for that environment). Once locked it won't change versions, even if you deploy new versions.
This simple GitHub action workflow will deploy your Trigger.dev tasks when new code is pushed to the `main` branch.
